critical_findings.title: RDS instance is publicly accessible with a hardcoded password
critical_findings.explanation: aws_db_instance.main sets publicly_accessible = true and hardcodes the master password in plaintext ('SuperSecret123!'). This exposes the database directly to the internet with a credential visible in source control.
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Set publicly_accessible = false, move the password into AWS Secrets Manager or use manage_master_user_password = true, and place the instance in a private subnet.
critical_findings.fixed_snippet:
resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
  identifier                  = "cloudops-demo-db"
  engine                      = "postgres"
  instance_class              = "db.r5.2xlarge"
  allocated_storage           = 100
  username                    = "admin"
  manage_master_user_password = true
  publicly_accessible         = false
  storage_encrypted           = true
  skip_final_snapshot         = false
}

critical_findings.title: Security group allows all inbound traffic from the internet
critical_findings.explanation: aws_security_group.web permits ingress on all ports (0-65535) from 0.0.0.0/0, effectively exposing every service on the instance to the public internet.
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Restrict ingress to only the specific ports the application needs (e.g. 443) and scope cidr_blocks to known ranges or a load balancer security group.

critical_findings.title: IAM policy grants unrestricted admin access
critical_findings.explanation: aws_iam_policy.admin_all uses Action = "*" and Resource = "*", granting full administrative access to anything the policy is attached to.
critical_findings.recommended_fix: Scope the policy to only the specific actions and resources required, following least privilege.

all_findings: ... critical findings above, plus high/medium/low findings from all four agents (S3 public access block disabled, RDS storage not encrypted, m5.4xlarge with no auto-scaling, single-AZ deployment with no failover, no CloudWatch alarms configured, oversized db.r5.2xlarge for demo workload, etc.) — truncated here for brevity, full array returned by the live API
recommended_improvements: [CRITICAL] RDS instance is publicly accessible with a hardcoded password → Set publicly_accessible = false and use Secrets Manager
[CRITICAL] Security group allows all inbound traffic from the internet → Restrict ingress to required ports only
[CRITICAL] IAM policy grants unrestricted admin access → Scope policy to least privilege
[HIGH] S3 bucket public access block fully disabled → Re-enable all four block_public_* settings
[HIGH] No auto-scaling group; single m5.4xlarge instance → Move to an Auto Scaling Group with min/max sizing
[MEDIUM] RDS storage not encrypted at rest → Set storage_encrypted = true
[MEDIUM] Single-AZ deployment with no failover → Enable Multi-AZ for aws_db_instance.main
[LOW] db.r5.2xlarge likely oversized for stated workload → Right-size to db.t3.large or add autoscaling storage
suggested_fix:
# Corrected excerpt addressing all CRITICAL/HIGH findings
resource "aws_security_group" "web" {
  name        = "web-sg"
  description = "Allow HTTPS only"

  ingress {
    from_port   = 443
    to_port     = 443
    protocol    = "tcp"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }

  egress {
    from_port   = 0
    to_port     = 0
    protocol    = "-1"
    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
  }
}

resource "aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block" "data" {
  bucket                  = aws_s3_bucket.data.id
  block_public_acls       = true
  block_public_policy     = true
  ignore_public_acls      = true
  restrict_public_buckets = true
}

resource "aws_db_instance" "main" {
  identifier                  = "cloudops-demo-db"
  engine                      = "postgres"
  instance_class              = "db.r5.2xlarge"
  allocated_storage           = 100
  username                    = "admin"
  manage_master_user_password = true
  publicly_accessible         = false
  storage_encrypted           = true
  multi_az                    = true
  skip_final_snapshot         = false
}
executive_summary: This Terraform configuration has an overall health score of 24/100 driven primarily by three critical security issues: a publicly accessible database with a hardcoded plaintext password, a security group open to all inbound traffic, and an IAM policy granting unrestricted admin access. Networking and reliability are moderately weak due to a single-AZ, single-instance deployment with no auto-scaling or failover. Cost efficiency is low because of oversized, statically provisioned compute (m5.4xlarge, db.r5.2xlarge) with no right-sizing. We recommend addressing the three critical findings immediately before this configuration touches any real environment.
